subject.title: [Bug]: Spurious "Something went wrong" and Codex app-server failures in large Telegram direct sessions

question: For a Codex turn that has uncertain terminal state or a session-resolution failure after partial/success-like output, should OpenClaw preserve the conservative verify-and-retry outcome while adding a precise diagnostic, or adopt an automatic restart/replay policy?
rationale: The implementation must balance clear user recovery against duplicate tool execution or repeated side effects; the incident evidence does not establish that an automatic retry is safe.

options.title: Conservative recovery with diagnostics
options.body: Keep non-replay behavior, add a stable error/run correlation path, and only suppress a fallback when delivery is conclusively known.

options.title: Automatic replay after classification
options.body: Restart only a narrowly classified no-side-effect failure path, with explicit idempotency and delivery-state proof.

options.title: Wait for exact-path evidence
options.body: Do not change recovery behavior until a current-version `sessions.resolve current` incident is captured with matched trajectory and gateway records.

recommendation.title: Conservative recovery with diagnostics
recommendation.body: Keep non-replay behavior, add a stable error/run correlation path, and only suppress a fallback when delivery is conclusively known.

likelyOwner.reason: The merged Codex lifecycle fix and its recovery semantics are the closest owner-boundary history for the decision.
